text:
jess_support: FYI customer sent over an urgent one — says they can log into the Console fine but any API calls with their project API key return 403. Customer: "console shows me as Project Owner, but curl /v1/predict -> 403"

jess_support: Posted repro and logs they provided below (redacted keys). Can someone triage? @mike_sre @olga_auth :thinking_face:

mike_sre: I can take a look. Quick Qs: org id + project id? Also, is this an API key created from Console (Project scope) or a service token created via platform API?

jess_support: Customer says created the key from the Console -> Project Settings -> API Keys yesterday. Org: org_8x8, Project: proj-zen-42.

jess_support: Customer repro (they redacted key):
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood-inference.net/v1/predict -d '{"model":"gpt-xyz","input":"hi"}'

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "reason": "project:write_required"
}
```

olga_auth: Hm. "project:write_required" implies the token doesn't have project write permission. Console can show web access while token scopes differ. Could be: (1) API key scoped incorrectly, (2) role propagation not applied to token, or (3) SCIM/group mapping gave the user a web-only role.

mike_sre: Checking audit + auth logs for proj-zen-42... grabbing token lookup now.

deploy-bot: iam-sync-run started at 2333333500 for org org_8x8

deploy-bot: iam-sync-run completed at 2333333525 with 1 warning (group mapping mismatch: group 'proj-zen-admins' -> mapped to role 'viewer' due to attribute mismatch)

mike_sre: Found the API key id they used in the request. It was created yesterday but bound to role viewer at creation time. The Console UI shows the user as Owner because the web session used the SSO claim (scim:role=owner) which was updated after the key was minted. The key's permission set didn't get backfilled.

jess_support: So the UI and API key are out of sync. Customer understandably confused. Any safe workaround to unblock them?

olga_auth: Short term: regenerate the API key after the SCIM sync resolves (or create a new key from Project Settings now). A created/minted key captures the effective role at creation time. If role changed later, existing keys won't auto-upgrade.

mike_sre: I'll run a manual resync and attempt to backfill key bindings where appropriate. If we can't safely change existing key scopes, we'll advise customer to create a new project-scoped key. Noted potential bug: iam-sync didn't apply role mapping for group 'proj-zen-admins' because the SCIM group external id changed. Filing a fix.

sam_product: Adding context for support docs: need an explainer that Console access != API key scopes and that keys are snapshot-of-role at creation. Could save some tickets.

jess_support: Messaged customer: please try creating a new API key from Project Settings and test, we'll also run an admin resync on our side and follow up.

jess_support: Customer responded — created a new key and confirms API calls now succeed (200).

mike_sre: Root cause summary: SCIM/group external_id change caused iam-sync to map group -> viewer instead of owner during one run, leaving an old key minted as viewer. Fix: patch iam-sync to be tolerant of external id aliases and perform a background backfill for API key role bindings.

olga_auth: Created issue INF-1429 and scheduled a hotfix for the mapping logic. Also adding a small UI tooltip: "API keys capture role at creation time".

jess_support: Marking as resolved for customer, leaving ticket open until INF-1429 deployed. Thanks everyone :heart:
